```{r}
caterpillar_data <- read.csv(here("data", "clean data", "caterpillar_data.csv"))

#caterpillar_data <- caterpillar_data %>%
  #filter(!is.na(hatch_date)) 

#save all weights as numbers not characters
caterpillar_data$pupal_treatment <- as.factor(caterpillar_data$pupal_treatment)
caterpillar_data$hatch_date <- as.Date(caterpillar_data$hatch_date)
caterpillar_data$weight_1 <- as.numeric(caterpillar_data$weight_1)
caterpillar_data$weight_2 <- as.numeric(caterpillar_data$weight_2)
caterpillar_data$weight3 <- as.numeric(caterpillar_data$weight3)
caterpillar_data$weight4 <- as.numeric(caterpillar_data$weight4)
caterpillar_data$weight_5 <- as.numeric(caterpillar_data$weight_5)
caterpillar_data$weight_6 <- as.numeric(caterpillar_data$weight_6)

#turn all weights into mg
caterpillar_data$weight_1 <- caterpillar_data$weight_1 * 1000
caterpillar_data$weight_2 <- caterpillar_data$weight_2 * 1000
caterpillar_data$weight3 <- caterpillar_data$weight3 * 1000
caterpillar_data$weight4 <- caterpillar_data$weight4 * 1000
caterpillar_data$weight_5 <- caterpillar_data$weight_5 * 1000
caterpillar_data$weight_6 <- caterpillar_data$weight_6 * 1000

#this dataset has 201 caterpillars but that is because AM321.07 appears twice. 
#this caterpillar died before pupation so it will be removed anyway

#save pupation date as a date
 caterpillar_data <- caterpillar_data %>%
   mutate(
    pupation_date = as.Date(pupation_date, format = "%m/%d/%Y")
  )


#how many eggs hatched
sum(!is.na(caterpillar_data$hatch_date))
#181 eggs hatched

#remove rows where hatched is NA, and where there are not at least two weights
caterpillar_data <- caterpillar_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(hatched)) %>% # remove those that didn't hatch
  filter(status == "hatched") #take only caterpillars that hatched. remove ones that were lost, crushed, squashed, unhatched or died


#remove this caterpillar because I made a mistake weighing it...
caterpillar_data <- caterpillar_data %>%
  filter(eggID != "AA297.06")


```

```{r}
#fix the names of the columns
names(caterpillar_data) <- names(caterpillar_data) %>%
  gsub("^weight([0-9]+)$", "weight_\\1", .)

#turn the data into long format
long_data <- caterpillar_data %>%
  mutate(id = row_number()) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^(weight|weighday)_\\d+$"),
    names_to = c(".value", "time"),
    names_pattern = "(weight|weighday)_(\\d+)"
  )

#save weighday as a date
long_data$weighday <- as.Date(
  parse_date_time(long_data$weighday, orders = c("ymd", "mdy"))
)

#add a days post hatch column
long_data <- long_data %>%
  mutate(days_post_hatch = as.numeric(weighday - hatch_date)) %>%
  filter(!is.na("weight"))

```

```{r}
#remove rows with NAs
long_data <- long_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(weight),
    !is.na(days_post_hatch),
    !is.na(eggID)
  ) %>%
  mutate("log_weight" = log(weight),
         "sqrt_weight" = sqrt(weight)) 


#group the data by eggID, and then for each eggID estimate the best-fitting line using a quadratic equation. then extract the coefficient of that line (the slope). This is the growth rate of that caterpillar.
slopes_non_linear <- long_data %>%
  group_by(eggID) %>%
  summarise(
    slope = coef(lm(log_weight ~ days_post_hatch + I(days_post_hatch^2)))[2])

mean(slopes_non_linear$slope)
sd(slopes_non_linear$slope)

```


```{r}
#TO MAKE A PLOT
# Fit a quadratic model for each caterpillar
quadratic_predictions <- long_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  group_modify(~ {

    # Fit the quadratic model
    model <- lm(
      log_weight ~ days_post_hatch + I(days_post_hatch^2),
      data = .x
    )

    # Generate many time points for a smooth curve
    new_data <- tibble(
      days_post_hatch = seq(
        min(.x$days_post_hatch),
        max(.x$days_post_hatch),
        length.out = 100
      )
    )

    # Predict weight at each time point
    new_data %>%
      mutate(log_weight = predict(model, newdata = new_data))
  }) %>%
  ungroup()


larval_growth <- ggplot() +
  
   # Quadratic curves
  geom_line(
    data = quadratic_predictions,
    aes(x = days_post_hatch, y = log_weight, group = id, colour = factor(id)),
    alpha = 0.6,
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  
  # Raw observations
  geom_point(
    data = long_data,
    aes(x = days_post_hatch, y = log_weight, colour = factor(id)),
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 3.0
  ) +
   scale_colour_viridis_d(option = "viridis") +

  labs(
    x = "Days post hatch",
    y = "log weight (mg)",
    title = "A) Larval growth "
  ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 30),            # increases all text
    axis.title = element_text(size = 30),      # axis titles bigger
    axis.text = element_text(size = 30),       # axis tick labels bigger
    legend.text = element_text(size = 30),     # legend text bigger
    legend.title = element_text(size = 30))

larval_growth
```




```{r}
#now i want to join this back onto the caterpillar_data spreadsheet
caterpillar_data <- caterpillar_data %>%
  left_join(slopes_non_linear, by = "eggID")

#mean and SD of slopes (growth rate)
mean(caterpillar_data$slope)
sd(caterpillar_data$slope)


#plot the relationship between growth rate and egg size
growth_rate <- ggplot(caterpillar_data, aes(x = size_01, y = slope)) +
  geom_point(size = 5) +
  labs( x = expression(Egg~area~(mm^2)), y = expression(Relative~growth~rate~(mg %.% mg^-1 %.% day^-1)), title = "B) Egg size vs larval growth rate") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0.18, 0.26, by = 0.02),
    limits = c(0.18, 0.26)) +
    theme(
    text = element_text(size = 30),            # increases all text
    axis.title = element_text(size = 30),      # axis titles bigger
    axis.text = element_text(size = 30),       # axis tick labels bigger
    legend.text = element_text(size = 30),     # legend text bigger
    legend.title = element_text(size = 30)
    )

growth_rate

#join together in a multi-panelled figure
caterpillar_plot <-  larval_growth + growth_rate

ggsave(
  here("figures", "figure 8 - growth rate figure.png"),
  plot = caterpillar_plot,
  width = 20,
  height = 10,
  dpi = 300
)

```
